### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e61af97294e85b99ad5a75c22693a500067f2c1f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fbae18854f28359b7c5b1c8ec05fcf714218afdd` — the merge of head `3e1e5d215c920e50c025f2ccef671e6c288d4058` into base `e61af97294e85b99ad5a75c22693a500067f2c1f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fbae18854f28359b7c5b1c8ec05fcf714218afdd && git checkout fbae18854f28359b7c5b1c8ec05fcf714218afdd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e61af97294e85b99ad5a75c22693a500067f2c1f 3e1e5d215c920e50c025f2ccef671e6c288d4058 && git checkout -B drift-repro e61af97294e85b99ad5a75c22693a500067f2c1f && git merge --no-ff 3e1e5d215c920e50c025f2ccef671e6c288d4058

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e61af97294e85b99ad5a75c22693a500067f2c1f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34663 · card #34616 (Fixes) · first review · L1-c2 of seat repo:objectstack#2 · read 2026-11-17T09:42Z

Read from GitHub and the diff at this head (merge base `e61af972`), not from the report. 6 files, +221/−13.

**Shape.** The PR is a draft against `main` and opens with `Fixes #34616`, which is right because the card's re-check (drop the dependency and the advisory returns) is met. The changeset is `patch` on `@objectstack/lint`, the one touched published package, and carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The CLI only gains a test, so it needs no changeset. No file outside the card is touched.

**Code**
- `dependencyClosureObjectNames` reads `packages[]` (`packagesOf`) and the stack's own `manifest.id`. It walks `resolvePackageClosure` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which is already a `workspace:*` dependency of `@objectstack/lint` and is re-exported by `runtime-gate.ts`. It adds the objects of `closure.dependencies` only.
- A sibling package the manifest did not declare, and a declared dependency the artifact does not carry, add nothing.
- The names are added only when `options.packageScope` is absent. Under a stated closure `stack.objects` already is the closure, so the publish-gate path is unchanged.
- Both readers of the set get the same answer: the trigger object (`flow-trigger-unknown-object`) and a record start input (`flow-input-unknown-object`).
- The change can only remove findings, never add one.

**Pins**
- The lint group has 7 cases: a declared dependency's object is clean; without the dependency the same flow warns `warning` at the trigger path; the closure is transitive; an uncarried dependency provides nothing; a misspelt name keeps its finding; the start-input position in both directions; and a stated closure keeps the `error`.
- The CLI test drives `runPerPackageAuthoringRules` (`command: 'lint'`) with the card's two-package fixture. Its CONTROL warns at `package 'com.example.psa' — flow "report_submitted" › start node`, and declaring the dependency clears it.
- The ablation (3/148 red) and the real `os lint --strict` table on `examples/app-multi-package` (main 4 warnings with the id, this PR 3 without, dependency dropped 4 with) are lane-reported, and I did not re-run them.

**Prose**, checked against the code above:
- The changeset's "A sibling package B did not declare still warns, and so does a name no package in the closure provides. Under a closure the publish gate states, nothing changes."
- Both `os explain` paragraphs: "counting the objects of the packages its manifest declares in `dependencies` when the artifact carries them".
- The `validating-metadata.mdx` sentence: "they resolve only through the packages the manifest declares in `dependencies` (transitively) … one on an undeclared sibling's object still warns".

All of these match. `skills/**` does not mention either rule id.

**Gates**: 68 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 58 `success`, 10 `skipped`, 0 failed. The lane's local suite and derived-gate readings (lint 9098/9098, 100 of 100 derived families run) were taken at `f2f2a845`/`87e47ab9`. The PR's own patch-id (`8441b2ee…`) is the same at this head, but those readings are pinned to the earlier heads. CI at this head is the reading of record.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: no `Clause-②: yes`, no narrowing, no `packages/spec/src`, no governed rule text. `content/docs/**` and the changeset are prose faces, checked above.

**Landing tier**: NOT governed (0 governed paths), +221/−13 = 234 lines, no spec face and no narrowing. **The area lands it** (ordinary queue landing).
